title: Adaptive Scaffolding for Cognitive Engagement in an Intelligent Tutoring System
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether an intelligent tutoring system can improve learning by adaptively changing the level of cognitive engagement required by worked examples. The authors frame the problem using the ICAP model, asking whether students should receive more guided, active examples or more buggy, constructive examples depending on their current knowledge. They compare two adaptive policies, one based on Bayesian Knowledge Tracing (BKT) and one based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), against a random non-adaptive control condition.

The intervention was implemented in an intelligent logic tutor for undergraduate discrete mathematics. Students worked through pretest, training, level-end tests, and posttest problems across seven levels. During training, the system selected among problem solving, Guided worked examples, and Buggy worked examples; the adaptive conditions changed the problem type based on estimated mastery or learned policy, while the control condition selected problem types at random. The study included 113 students at a U.S. public university, with analyses reported for the 113 who completed all seven levels.

Results showed that both adaptive conditions significantly improved posttest performance compared with the control group, with similar overall effect sizes. BKT especially helped lower-prior-knowledge students close the gap with higher-prior-knowledge peers, while DRL more strongly favored guided examples and produced comparable learning gains. The authors conclude that adaptively varying cognitive engagement in an ITS can improve learning outcomes, and that adaptation itself may matter more than the specific algorithm used in this study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a controlled between-subjects classroom study with stratified assignment and statistical analyses, but it is not a randomized controlled trial in the strictest sense and is limited to one tutor and one course context. The design is credible but has some generalizability and implementation constraints, so green is appropriate.
impact_tier_rationale: The adaptive ITS conditions produced modest-to-moderate gains on posttest scores (A=.58) and small efficiency improvements, indicating meaningful but not large effects. Because the setting is a single undergraduate logic course rather than a broad K-12 population, the practical impact is promising but not high.

interventions.use_case: adaptive logic tutoring with problem solving, guided worked examples, and buggy worked examples selected by Bayesian Knowledge Tracing or deep reinforcement learning

finding.finding_summary: In a controlled between-subjects study with 113 students (analyzed n=113; 36 Control, 35 BKT, 42 DRL), both adaptive tutoring policies improved posttest performance on a logic tutor relative to random assignment. Posttest composite scores were higher for BKT (M=72.3) and DRL (M=72.5) than Control (M=65.7), with probability-based effect sizes of A=.58 for both comparisons (BKT p=.005; DRL p=.002).
finding.measure: Posttest composite problem score (rule accuracy, solution length, and completion time) and normalized learning gain
finding.confidence_interval: 95% CI [.52, .63] for BKT vs Control; [.53, .64] for DRL vs Control

finding.finding_summary: The paper substantively examines cognitive engagement/adaptive scaffolding as a durable-skill mechanism, showing that adaptive selection of worked examples by prior knowledge improved learning outcomes and efficiency. The BKT condition also reduced posttest completion time relative to Control (10.8 vs 11.8 minutes per problem, p=.02, A=.58), while DRL showed a marginal time reduction (10.7 vs 11.8 minutes, p=.06, A=.56), suggesting improved task efficiency alongside learning gains.
finding.measure: Posttest problem completion time and solution optimality (number of steps)
finding.effect_size: A=.58 (time, BKT vs Control); A=.56 (time/steps, DRL vs Control)
finding.confidence_interval: 95% CI [.53, .63] for BKT time; [.51, .61] for DRL time/steps
